Paper_name: The self can be associated with novel faces of in-group and out-group members: A cross-cultural study
Summary: This study investigated whether the self can be associated with faces of unknown people from different ethnic groups. Two experiments were conducted: one with Asian Japanese participants and another with White Italian participants. Both groups completed a perceptual matching task associating themselves with either Asian or White faces. The results showed a reliable self-association with facial stimuli, which was similar for both in-group and out-group faces. Furthermore, no correlation was found between the strength of this association and an index of implicit racial bias.
Author: Mario Dalmaso, Michele Vicovaro, Akira Sarodo, Katsumi Watanabe
Conclusion: The self is malleable and can incorporate social stimuli from different ethnic groups. A reliable self-prioritisation effect was found when associating the self with faces, and this effect was not modulated by the ethnicity (in-group vs. out-group) of the faces. The strength of this association was not correlated with implicit racial bias measures.
